name: Video Transcriber
tagline: Upload a video file or paste a public link, get a searchable transcript with speaker labels and subtitle exports.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This category sits on top of open weights, which is the whole story. Whisper (or faster-whisper, or whisper.cpp) plus ffmpeg plus yt-dlp covers file ingest, link ingest, transcription, and timestamped output, and the export formats are string formatting, not engineering. Speaker labels are the one genuinely annoying part: pyannote needs a Hugging Face token and gated model acceptance, and its accuracy on crosstalk is mediocre everywhere, including in paid products. If you process video occasionally and own a machine with a GPU or just patience, a local version is a single session of work and costs nothing per minute forever. The reason to pay is that you want a URL box in a browser tab and no Python in your life.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that takes an uploaded video or a public URL, extracts audio with ffmpeg, transcribes with faster-whisper, optionally diarizes with pyannote, and exports TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT, and CSV.
requirements: A machine with a decent CPU, GPU strongly preferred for long videos
Hugging Face token and accepted model terms if you want speaker diarization
Disk space for model weights, roughly 1 to 3 GB depending on model size
whatYouLose: No queue: a two hour video ties up your laptop instead of someone's GPU fleet
Speaker diarization setup is gated behind Hugging Face token plumbing and is fiddly to get right
No polished browser editor for fixing transcript errors and re-syncing timings
Link ingest breaks whenever a platform changes its player, and yt-dlp updates are your problem
Nothing to share: no links, no team access, no mobile upload from a phone
moatNotes: The model is open, so the product is the convenience layer: a fast queue, a usable editor, and formats that actually validate.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because transcription is bursty. Most people need it four times a year, usually under deadline, usually on a laptop that is already doing something else, and paying a few dollars to have a transcript in ten minutes beats installing CUDA at 11pm. The paid versions also absorb the two boring failure modes: long files that need chunking and resumption, and subtitle files that have to be frame-accurate enough for an editor to accept them.
notes: The entire industry here is a UI wrapper around weights that Meta and OpenAI gave away, and most of them know it.
prompt:
Build a local video transcription tool. Single machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, server-rendered Jinja2 templates with plain HTML and a little vanilla JS. No React. SQLite via sqlite3 for job records. Store everything under ./data.

Core flow:
1. A single page with two inputs: a file upload (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, mp3, wav, m4a) and a text field for a public video URL.
2. URL ingest uses yt-dlp as a Python module to download audio only. File uploads are saved to ./data/uploads.
3. Extract and normalize audio with ffmpeg via subprocess: mono, 16 kHz, 16-bit WAV.
4. Transcribe with faster-whisper. Default model size from WHISPER_MODEL in .env, default "small". Auto-detect device: cuda if available, else cpu with int8 compute type. Request word timestamps.
5. Optional speaker labels: if HF_TOKEN is set in .env, run pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 and assign each segment the speaker whose turn overlaps it most. If HF_TOKEN is missing, skip diarization silently and label everything "Speaker". Do not crash.
6. Run jobs in a background thread with a simple in-process queue, one at a time. Poll job status from the page every 2 seconds and show stage plus percent where known.

Outputs, all generated from one internal segment list (start, end, speaker, text):
- TXT: plain paragraphs, speaker prefix when diarization ran
- SRT and VTT: correctly formatted timestamps, max 2 lines and ~42 chars per cue, split on word boundaries using word timestamps
- CSV: start,end,speaker,text with proper quoting
- DOCX: via python-docx, speaker headings and body text
Write exports to ./data/exports/{job_id}/ and expose download links.

Also build a transcript view page with the segments listed, a search box that filters segments client-side, and a click-to-copy button.

Out of scope: user accounts, payments, translation, an editable transcript editor, multi-machine workers, anything touching private or login-walled video URLs.

Deliver: requirements.txt, .env.example with WHISPER_MODEL and HF_TOKEN, a README with ffmpeg install notes per OS and a realistic speed table for cpu versus cuda, and one end-to-end smoke test using a 10 second generated sine-wave video so the test suite needs no network.
